host-debugging discipline (user's own host, remote/blind): (1) NEVER modify before the diagnosis is complete — read the FULL error/journal output first: a journalctl paste showed 3 broken apparmor profiles (usr.sbin.libvirtd:145, libvirt-qemu via openssl chain, virt-aa-helper:91) and only 2 were fixed while the third was visible in the same log; (2) never use apparmor_parser -Q (skip-kernel-load) as a diagnostic: without kernel ABI detection it false-fails on valid abi<4.0> abstraction lines and created a ghost problem; (3) rules appended via tee -a to a PROFILE file land AFTER the closing brace = parse error — know the file structure before appending; (4) AppArmor on non-NixOS + Nix binaries: libvirtd profile denies exec of nix-store paths — per-VM profiles need rules in local/abstractions/libvirt-qemu (mr) and daemon profile needs rix incl. the dot-wrapped nix binary (.qemu-system-x86_64-wrapped); complain mode (force-complain symlink or aa-complain) is the correct unblock-then-collect-denials workflow. Session context: virt-manager+Nix QEMU 11.1.1 on Mint 22, kernel 7.0 HWE required (>=6.13) for venus.
